guide.title: Incident Command System
guide.lead: ICS gives every incident the same shape, so people from different services can slot in. Know who you report to, stay in your role, and use plain language. As an EMS provider you will usually work in the Medical Branch of Operations: triage, treatment, transport or staging.

flashcards.question: Incident Command System
flashcards.answer: A standard, all-hazards, on-scene structure that expands and contracts with the incident.

flashcards.question: Span of control
flashcards.answer: 3–7 people per supervisor, about 5 ideal. More than 7: add a supervisor.

flashcards.question: Command Staff
flashcards.answer: Three positions: Safety Officer, Public Information Officer, Liaison Officer.

flashcards.question: General Staff sections
flashcards.answer: Four: Operations, Planning, Logistics, Finance/Administration. Intelligence/Investigations may be added as a fifth.

flashcards.question: Where EMS works in ICS
flashcards.answer: Operations Section, Medical Branch: triage, treatment, transport, staging.

flashcards.question: Area vs Unified Command
flashcards.answer: Area Command oversees several separate incidents. Unified Command: several agencies share command of one incident with one plan.

flashcards.question: Safety Officer authority
flashcards.answer: Can stop any operation with an imminent danger, outside the normal chain of command.

flashcards.question: Demobilisation
flashcards.answer: Orderly, safe release of resources; nobody leaves without being released and checking out.

critical.scenario: You're in the red treatment area after a tornado. A volunteer tells you the 'Incident Commander' wants you to go and search houses.
critical.question: How do you respond?

options.t: Stay in role and check the order through your supervisor (Treatment Unit Leader); move only if it's confirmed

options.f: Unverified orders break unity of command.

options.t: Send your patients to the volunteer

critical.explanation: Freelancing leaves gaps and puts people at risk.
critical.kpi: Maintains unity of command and chain of command

critical.scenario: You're Staging Manager. Operations wants 4 ambulances; you have 8 – but a fire captain has already sent all 8 to the scene without telling you, and 12 more patients need transport.
critical.question: Response?

options.t: Tell Operations staging is empty, request more ambulances, and raise the freelancing through the chain of command
Drive patients in your own car

critical.explanation: Accurate resource status is the point of staging.
critical.kpi: Communicates resource status and addresses freelancing

critical.scenario: Unified Command at an apartment fire. A police officer orders you to leave your treatment area and move patients to a bus.
critical.question: What do you do?

options.t: Politely decline and refer him to the Treatment Unit Leader; follow your own chain of command

options.f: Rank doesn't override the ICS chain.

critical.explanation: Unified Command shares decisions at the top; everyone else follows one supervisor.
critical.kpi: Applies unity of command within unified command
